All sodium, potassium and ammonium compounds, and all nitrates.

notes: All other common chlorides are soluble.

back: Barium sulfate, calcium sulfate and lead(II) sulfate.
Only sodium, potassium and ammonium carbonates.
Sodium, potassium and ammonium hydroxides; calcium hydroxide is partially soluble.

front: How is an insoluble salt prepared?
back: Mix solutions of two soluble salts, filter, wash the precipitate with distilled water and dry it.

front: Which reagents supply the ions for a precipitation?
back: Usually the metal's nitrate and the sodium or potassium salt of the negative ion (both always soluble).
notes: Example: lead(II) nitrate + potassium iodide → lead(II) iodide.
